answer: Activation is earned, not issued: a fresh identity stays dormant until its owner completes a sonnet of fourteen dated proofs, one per day, stitched into a single unbroken thread. The registry lays out those fourteen days as a trellis of fixed dated slots, so a proof only counts in its own slot; a missed day resets the thread to zero, and backdating is impossible because peers timestamp each proof as it lands. Forging 1,000 puppets takes 14,000 daily proofs at one agent-hour each, while one honest applicant spends fourteen ten-minute check-ins.
